mechanism: Bioresorbable intravitreal hydrogel implant incorporating axitinib, a small-molecule multi-target tyrosine kinase inhibitor with anti-angiogenic activity and company-described pan-VEGF receptor inhibition.
development_status: NCT06223958/SOL-1 is an active-not-recruiting Phase 3 superiority trial in treatment-naive wet AMD with 344 actual randomized subjects. Ocular reported positive Week 36 and Week 52 SOL-1 data in February 2026 and states that an NDA based on SOL-1 Week 52 data remains on track, subject to ongoing or planned formal FDA discussions. A second Phase 3 wet AMD trial, NCT06495918/SOL-R, is active not recruiting and is expected by the company to read out in 1Q 2027.
expected_launch_window: Potential U.S. 2027 launch if NDA submission, FDA acceptance, review, and approval proceed on the company's planned SOL-1-based path; timing remains contingent on FDA discussions and review.
clinical_summary: AXPAXLI is differentiated by a durable intravitreal TKI implant approach rather than repeated soluble anti-VEGF biologic injections. In SOL-1, after two aflibercept loading doses, one AXPAXLI 0.45 mg implant met the Week 36 superiority endpoint versus one aflibercept 2 mg injection: 74.1% versus 55.8% maintained vision, with p=0.0006. Week 52 durability was also statistically significant at 65.9% versus 44.2%, p<0.0001. AXPAXLI rescue-free rates were 80.6%, 74.7%, and 68.8% at Weeks 24, 36, and 52, and Ocular positions the product as potentially reducing treatment burden through annual or six-month-style dosing paradigms. Differentiation is high, but FDA review, final label, repeat-dosing data, rescue criteria, and real-world adherence will determine commercial scope.
safety_summary: ClinicalTrials.gov has no posted results for NCT06223958, but Ocular reported that, as of the February 5, 2026 Week 52 database lock, AXPAXLI was generally well tolerated in SOL-1 with no observed treatment-related ocular or systemic serious adverse events. The company also reported no endophthalmitis, occlusive or non-occlusive retinal vasculitis, retinal detachment, or implant migration to the anterior chamber in the AXPAXLI arm. Safety follow-up continues through Week 104, with re-dosing at Weeks 52 and 76. Intravitreal anti-VEGF analog labels support ongoing attention to endophthalmitis, retinal detachment, intraocular inflammation, intraocular pressure increases, retinal vasculitis/vascular occlusion, and arterial thromboembolic events.
management_tools: Medical-benefit prior authorization tied to FDA-labeled wet AMD criteria, active CNV documentation, and treated-eye specificity
Dose and frequency limits aligned to final label, treated eye count, re-dosing interval, and rescue-therapy language
Baseline and renewal documentation of BCVA, OCT/CSFT or retinal fluid, prior anti-VEGF loading or response, and rescue-injection need
Step or preferred-product criteria versus lower-cost bevacizumab or preferred anti-VEGF products only if compatible with final indication, FDA label, and evidence
Avoid same-eye concomitant intravitreal anti-VEGF/TKI therapy except for label-supported rescue treatment
Specialty distributor or buy-and-bill controls for acquisition, inventory, wastage, and site-of-care billing
Launch monitoring for bilateral use, rescue aflibercept utilization, re-dosing intervals, and adverse-event claims
evidence_gaps: No FDA approval, U.S. prescribing information, NDA acceptance, PDUFA date, or direct AXPAXLI price was identified.
ClinicalTrials.gov has no posted results for NCT06223958, NCT06495918, NCT04989699, or NCT03630315.

The planned NDA path based on SOL-1 remains subject to FDA discussions; Ocular acknowledges uncertainty over whether FDA will accept a single-pivotal-trial NDA and whether the SOL-1 package is sufficient for approval.
SOL-R repeat-dosing/non-inferiority data are not yet available; company guidance points to 1Q 2027 topline data.
Final label may differ from trial protocols, including loading requirements, treatment-naive positioning, rescue criteria, re-dosing interval, and bilateral use.
Annual cost is analog-derived from EYLEA HD WAC because AXPAXLI is investigational and unpriced.

sources.title: Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Intravitreal OTX-TKI (Ocular Therapeutix) (Axitinib Implant) in Subjects With Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration
supports: SOL-1 official title is a Phase 3 multicenter, double-masked, randomized, parallel-group study of intravitreal OTX-TKI axitinib implant in nAMD.
Sponsor is Ocular Therapeutix, Inc.; the study is FDA-regulated as a drug trial.
Overall status is active, not recruiting; actual enrollment is 344; actual start date is 2024-01-29.
Primary completion is estimated 2026-04-29 and study completion is estimated 2027-09-27.
Arms are OTX-TKI axitinib implant and aflibercept control.
Primary endpoint is BCVA maintenance, defined as less than 15 ETDRS-letter BCVA loss, up to 36 weeks.
Other safety outcome is incidence and severity of treatment-emergent adverse events up to 104 weeks.
ClinicalTrials.gov hasResults is false.

sources.title: Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Intravitreal OTX-TKI (Axitinib Implant) in Subjects With Neovascular Age- Related Macular Degeneration
supports: SOL-R is a Phase 3 randomized, double-masked, parallel-group study of OTX-TKI in neovascular age-related macular degeneration.
Overall status is active, not recruiting; estimated enrollment is 825; actual start date is 2024-11-27.
Arms include OTX-TKI re-dose, aflibercept 2 mg on-label, and aflibercept 8 mg high-dose comparators.
Primary endpoint is mean change in BCVA from baseline at Week 48.
ClinicalTrials.gov hasResults is false.

sources.title: Study Evaluating the Treatment of OTX-TKI for Subjects With Neovascular Age-related Macular Degeneration
supports: Completed U.S. Phase 1 randomized study sponsored by Ocular Therapeutix.
Actual enrollment was 21 and study completion was 2023-12-18.
Study evaluated safety, tolerability, and efficacy of OTX-TKI for intravitreal use in nAMD.
OTX-TKI arm involved one dose with sham at subsequent visits to maintain masking; comparator aflibercept was administered every 8 weeks.
Primary endpoint was safety and tolerability through study completion; secondary endpoints included BCVA, central subfield thickness, rescue therapy, absence of fluid, and number of injections.
ClinicalTrials.gov hasResults is false.

sources.title: CLN-0046: Treatment of AMD Subjects With OTX-TKI
supports: Completed Phase 1 open-label dose-escalation study of OTX-TKI for intravitreal use in neovascular AMD.
Actual enrollment was 29; actual start was 2019-02-18; completion was 2024-01-10.
Primary endpoint was incidence of treatment-emergent adverse events for each subject over 9 months.
ClinicalTrials.gov hasResults is false.

sources.title: Ocular Therapeutix Pipeline
supports: Ocular lists AXPAXLI, also known as OTX-TKI, as an investigational axitinib hydrogel administered by intravitreal injection.
Wet AMD is listed in Phase 3 registrational development.
Ocular states AXPAXLI targets with axitinib, described as a highly potent TKI with strong selectivity for pan-VEGF receptor inhibition.
Ocular states the product is delivered with ELUTYX proprietary fully bioresorbable hydrogel technology.

sources.title: Ocular Therapeutix Reports Positive Results from Landmark SOL-1 Phase 3 Superiority Trial in Wet AMD
supports: SOL-1 compared a single dose of AXPAXLI 0.45 mg to a single aflibercept 2 mg dose after loading in wet AMD patients.
The trial met the Week 36 superiority primary endpoint with 74.1% of AXPAXLI subjects maintaining vision versus 55.8% of aflibercept subjects; risk difference 17.5%; p=0.0006.
Week 52 durability assessment was 65.9% maintaining vision for AXPAXLI versus 44.2% for aflibercept; risk difference 21.1%; p<0.0001.
AXPAXLI rescue-free rates were 80.6%, 74.7%, and 68.8% at Weeks 24, 36, and 52.

The AXPAXLI arm had no observed treatment-related ocular or systemic serious adverse events and no endophthalmitis, retinal vasculitis, retinal detachment, or anterior-chamber implant migration events.
Subjects were re-dosed at Week 52 and are planned for re-dosing at Week 76 with safety follow-up through Week 104.
Ocular intends to submit an NDA based on SOL-1 data, subject to formal FDA discussions.
Ocular states SOL-R topline data are expected in 1Q 2027.

sources.title: Ocular Therapeutix Reports First Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Business Highlights
supports: Commercial preparedness plans accelerated as Ocular intends to submit an AXPAXLI NDA based on SOL-1 Week 52 data, subject to ongoing formal FDA discussions.
SOL-R Phase 3 non-inferiority trial in wet AMD is on track for topline readout in 1Q 2027.
SOL-X long-term extension enrollment began in April 2026 for subjects completing two-year follow-up in SOL-1 or SOL-R.
Ocular states AXPAXLI NDA submission for wet AMD remains on track and that it plans to leverage the 505(b)(2) application pathway, which could potentially shorten review by up to two months.
SOL-R completed randomization of 631 subjects in December 2025, exceeding the company's 555-subject target.
Ocular reported selling and marketing expense increases tied to expansion of the commercial team and pre-commercial activities for AXPAXLI.

sources.title: DailyMed - EYLEA HD (aflibercept) injection, solution
supports: EYLEA HD is indicated for neovascular wet age-related macular degeneration.
EYLEA HD is administered by intravitreal injection by a qualified physician.
nAMD dosing is 8 mg every 4 weeks for the first three doses, followed by 8 mg every 8 to 16 weeks; every-20-week dosing may be considered after one year of successful response.
Warnings include endophthalmitis, retinal detachment, retinal vasculitis with or without occlusion, intraocular pressure increase, and thromboembolic events.
Used as current wet AMD intravitreal anti-VEGF label analog for safety and cost frequency assumptions.

sources.title: EYLEA HD Colorado Drug Cost Education
supports: EYLEA HD 8 mg single-dose vial and vial kit WAC price is $2,812.98.
WAC is the manufacturer's undiscounted list price to wholesalers and does not represent actual transaction prices, discounts, rebates, or reductions.
Pricing is stated as of 2026-01-09.
Used as current branded intravitreal wet AMD cost analog because no direct AXPAXLI price is available.

sources.title: Cigna Drug Coverage Policy: Ophthalmology - Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor Inhibitors - Vabysmo
supports: Cigna requires prior authorization for Vabysmo benefit coverage.
Vabysmo is considered medically necessary for neovascular wet AMD when policy criteria and dosing are met.
Approval requires administration by or under the supervision of an ophthalmologist and preferred-product criteria.
Dosing limits require 6 mg intravitreal injection for each treated eye and no more frequent than once every 4 weeks per treated eye.
Policy excludes concomitant use with another intravitreal VEGF inhibitor.
Supports likely management tools for future intravitreal wet AMD therapies.

expected_launch_window.value: Potential U.S. 2027 launch if NDA submission, FDA acceptance, review, and approval proceed on the company's planned SOL-1-based path; timing remains contingent on FDA discussions and review.
expected_launch_window.method: Used company statements that NDA submission based on SOL-1 Week 52 data remains on track, potential 505(b)(2) review efficiency, ongoing FDA discussions, and SOL-R 1Q 2027 topline guidance.
expected_launch_window.explanation: A 2027 window is plausible because SOL-1 is positive and Ocular is preparing an NDA, but the packet should not assume approval before FDA accepts the filing path, reviews the single-trial package, and resolves CMC/label questions.

annual_cost_range.method: No AXPAXLI price is available. Used EYLEA HD branded intravitreal wet AMD analog WAC of $2,812.98. Low assumes annual cost benchmark equivalent to four EYLEA HD doses, approximating extended 12-16 week maintenance. High assumes eight EYLEA HD doses, approximating higher-intensity first-year or frequent maintenance use. Values are rounded from $11,251.92 and $22,503.84.
annual_cost_range.explanation: This is a gross drug-acquisition planning proxy, not a forecast of AXPAXLI list price or net payer cost. Final cost may differ materially if Ocular prices the durable implant at a premium to annual anti-VEGF drug spend, if bilateral use is common, or if rescue aflibercept and administration costs are included.

clinical_differentiation.method: Weighted the novel durable intravitreal TKI implant mechanism, FDA-aligned Phase 3 superiority result versus aflibercept 2 mg, statistically significant Week 52 durability, rescue-free rates, and company-reported favorable serious-safety profile against pending FDA review and missing SOL-R readout.
clinical_differentiation.explanation: AXPAXLI has late-stage evidence for a differentiated wet AMD profile: superiority and durability with fewer rescue injections. The rating remains tied to source-backed SOL-1 data, with final differentiation dependent on label, repeat dosing, and real-world safety.

budget_impact.method: Combined analog branded intravitreal wet AMD annual cost, broad U.S. wet AMD prevalence and chronic treatment need, potential rapid adoption after a superiority label, bilateral-treatment potential, rescue-treatment add-ons, and medical-benefit buy-and-bill complexity.
budget_impact.explanation: Even if annual drug cost resembles current high-cost anti-VEGF therapy, a broad wet AMD label and reduced injection burden could drive rapid switching and meaningful medical-benefit spend concentration.

disruption_risk.method: Assessed positive registrational data, planned NDA, durable annual/six-month-style dosing potential, reduced rescue burden, first potential wet AMD TKI positioning, and impact on retina practice acquisition, scheduling, monitoring, and anti-VEGF utilization.
disruption_risk.explanation: AXPAXLI could materially change wet AMD treatment cadence and payer controls if approved. Disruption is high despite remaining regulatory uncertainty because commercial preparedness and pivotal data are already in place.

recommended_action.method: Matched action intensity to positive Phase 3 SOL-1, planned NDA path, ongoing pre-commercial activity, potential 2027 launch, and likely need for new policy, coding, billing, and rescue-therapy rules.
recommended_action.explanation: Begin draft coverage and operations planning now, while keeping assumptions provisional until FDA filing status, label, pricing, HCPCS/J-code strategy, SOL-R data, and launch timing are clarified.

quality_flags: No direct AXPAXLI price found; annual cost is derived from EYLEA HD WAC analog pricing.
No FDA approval, NDA acceptance, PDUFA date, or final U.S. label was identified as of 2026-05-28.
ClinicalTrials.gov does not post results for the included OTX-TKI studies; SOL-1 efficacy and safety results are company-reported.
The planned SOL-1-based NDA remains contingent on formal FDA discussions and acceptance of the filing package.
SOL-R repeat-dosing/non-inferiority results are pending, with company-guided topline readout in 1Q 2027.
Commercial dosing, rescue-therapy rules, bilateral-treatment assumptions, coding, reimbursement, and real-world adherence impact remain uncertain.
